name: Halo
author: E. T. Carter
description: Total solar eclipse: a dark occulting moon hangs high against a slow-twinkling starfield while a bright corona blazes around its limb, its edge frayed by ridged noise into the filamental streamers and prominences of a real eclipse. A thin warm chromosphere rings the limb and a diamond-ring point flares at one side. The corona crawls slowly around the disc, the radius breathes, and the streamers shimmer — all very slow, nothing that resets.

params.label: Moon radius
params.effect: CSS-pixel radius of the occulting moon, from a small distant eclipse to a frame-filling one with a sprawling corona.

params.label: Corona reach
params.effect: Depth and reach of the corona streamers — 0 leaves a tight ring at the limb, 2 streams long feathery prominences far out into space.

params.label: Waver speed
params.effect: How fast the corona streamers crawl around the disc and shimmer.

params.label: Star density
params.effect: How thickly stars fill the surrounding deep space — 0 is an empty void, 2 a dense crowded field.

params.label: Moon X
params.effect: Horizontal position of the eclipse across the frame, as a fraction of width.

params.label: Moon Y
params.effect: Vertical position of the eclipse, as a fraction of height (0 bottom, 1 top).
